name: Japanese Soboro Don (Sweet Soy Beef and Egg Rice Bowls)
ingredients: Oyster Sauce (Lee Kum Kee): 0.5 cups (126 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice according to the package and set it aside to steam.

Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt, melt the butter in a wide skillet over low heat, and cook the eggs slowly, stirring constantly with chopsticks or a fork so they break into fine soft crumbles rather than one sheet.
Scrape the egg crumbles out and set them aside.
Heat the vegetable oil in the same pan and cook the garlic briefly until fragrant.
Add the ground beef, break it up very fine, and cook until browned with no pink remaining.
Pour in the soy sauce, mirin, oyster sauce, and sugar, and simmer until the liquid reduces and glazes the beef.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste and slice the green onions for the top.

name: Japanese Turkey Nikujaga (Meat and Potato Stew)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the turkey breast into thin strips. Thin is important, because strips soak up the broth while chunks just sit in it.
Peel the potatoes and cut them into large chunks, slice the carrots on a diagonal, and cut the onion into thick wedges.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large heavy pot and sear the turkey strips until they lose their pink, then add the onion wedges and cook 3 minutes.
Add the potatoes and carrots, then pour in the chicken broth, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar. The liquid should come most of the way up the vegetables but not drown them.
Bring it to a simmer, then lay a round of parchment right on the surface and cover the pot. That paper lid is the Japanese trick that keeps everything basted without boiling the potatoes apart.
Simmer on low for 25 to 30 minutes until the potatoes are fork tender and the turkey has reached 165F, shaking the pot instead of stirring so nothing breaks up.
Add the green beans in the last 5 minutes, then let the pot sit off the heat for 15 minutes, which is when the potatoes actually drink up the broth.

name: John Wayne Casserole
ingredients: Diced Green Chiles (Old El Paso): 1.2 cans (139 g)
Diced Tomatoes & Green Chilies (Great Value (Ro-Tel style)): 1.2 cans (347 g)
Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 12.25 oz (346 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Press the biscuit dough into a greased 9x13 pan (plus a small second pan if needed) to form a solid crust, and bake at 350 F for about 10 minutes so it sets.
Brown the ground beef with most of the diced onion in your pot until no pink remains, then drain. Stir in the taco seasoning with a splash of water.
Add the diced tomatoes with green chilies and the diced green chiles. Simmer 5 minutes until thick.
In a bowl, mix the sour cream, mayonnaise, half the cheddar, and the remaining onion.
Layer beef over the biscuit crust, add the bell pepper, spread the sour cream mixture on top, and finish with the rest of the cheddar.
Bake at 350 F for 20 to 25 minutes until the cheese is melted and the edges bubble.

name: Johnny Marzetti Casserole
ingredients: Egg Noodles (Great Value wide): 26.5 oz dry (749 g)
Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 7.25 oz (208 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the egg noodles two minutes short of the package time, drain, and set aside. They finish cooking in the oven.
Brown the ground beef and ground pork with the diced onion in your big pot over medium-high heat until no pink remains. Drain excess fat.
Add the diced bell peppers and sliced mushrooms and cook 5 minutes until they soften.
Stir in the diced tomatoes, brown sugar, dijon, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Simmer 10 minutes so the sauce thickens up.
Fold in the noodles, olives, and half the cheddar until everything is coated.
Spread into a greased 9x13 pan (it will be full) or two smaller pans, top with the rest of the cheddar, and bake at 350 F for about 20 minutes until bubbly and melted.

name: Kadai Chicken (Chicken Karahi)
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 3.75 lb (1750 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Make the kadai masala: toast the dried chiles and the ground coriander in a dry pan for a minute, then crush them coarsely with the ground cumin, garam masala, italian seasoning and ground cinnamon. Coarse, not powdered.
Melt the butter in your largest heavy pan over medium-high and cook the sliced onion for 8 to 10 minutes until browned at the edges.

Add the garlic and cook a minute, then add the tomato sauce, chili powder, ground turmeric and salt. Cook this down hard for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring, until the sauce darkens and you can see butter pooling at the edges. That separation is the whole technique.
Add the chicken thighs cut into chunks and turn them in the masala. Cook uncovered 15 to 20 minutes, stirring often, until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce is clinging rather than pooling.
Stir in most of the crushed kadai masala and the sliced green bell pepper and cook 4 more minutes, so the pepper stays crisp instead of collapsing.
Turn off the heat and stir in the heavy cream and the chopped cilantro. Save a pinch of the crushed masala to scatter over the top.
Cook the rice separately, let it steam covered for 10 minutes, and fold it into the pot so every serving gets curry and rice together.

name: Lebanese Baked Kafta and Potatoes (Kafta bil Sanieh)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Mix the ground beef with finely diced onion, garlic, eggs, bread crumbs, ground allspice, ground cinnamon, salt, and black pepper until it just comes together.
Press the beef mixture in an even layer across the bottom of a large greased baking tray and bake it alone at 400 degrees until it firms up and releases its fat.
Pour off the rendered fat while the beef par-bakes, then peel and slice the potatoes into even rounds.
Toss the potato rounds with the vegetable oil, salt, and black pepper and layer them over the beef.
Scatter sliced green bell peppers over the potatoes.
Whisk the diced tomatoes and tomato paste with a little water into a loose sauce and pour it evenly across the tray.
Cover with foil and bake until the potatoes are completely tender, then uncover and bake until the top browns and the sauce tightens.

name: Kenyan Beef Pilau
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and let it drain, which keeps the grains separate.

Heat the vegetable oil in a large heavy pot and cook the sliced red onions over medium heat, patiently, until they go deep brown. This takes longer than you want it to and it is the most important step.
Add the garlic, ginger, and minced jalapeno and cook until fragrant.
Stir in the ground cumin, ground cloves, ground cinnamon, garam masala, black pepper, and bay leaves and let them toast in the oil for a minute.
Add the cubed beef and brown it on all sides, then add the diced tomatoes and cook until the sauce darkens and thickens.
Add the cubed potatoes and the beef broth, bring to a boil, then stir in the drained rice and season with salt.
Cover tightly, drop the heat as low as it goes, and cook undisturbed until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender, then rest ten minutes off the heat and fluff with the chopped cilantro.

name: Kerala Beef Ularthiyathu (South Indian Beef Fry) Rice Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the beef chuck roast into bite sized cubes.
Toss the beef with the chili powder, ground coriander, ground turmeric, black pepper, garam masala, ground fennel, salt, most of the garlic, most of the ginger, and the diced yellow onion.
Pressure cook the seasoned beef with a small splash of water until it is completely tender, then open it up and boil off any remaining liquid.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wide heavy pan and cook the sliced red onions and sliced jalapenos slowly until deeply browned and sweet.
Add the rest of the garlic and ginger and cook until fragrant.

Add the cooked beef and dry-roast it over medium heat, stirring and scraping, until the moisture is gone and the meat is dark and crusted at the edges. This takes patience and it is where the dish is made.
Taste for salt, then cook the rice according to the package to serve underneath.

name: Kharcho (Georgian Beef and Walnut Rice Soup)
ingredients: Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 0.5 tbsp (3 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the chuck into small cubes and simmer them in salted water for about 75 minutes, skimming the foam, until tender. Keep the broth in the pot.
In a separate pan, cook the chopped onion in the vegetable oil until soft and just golden.
Grind the walnuts to a coarse paste. A food processor is easiest, but a bag and a rolling pin works.
Stir the onions, ground walnuts, and diced tomatoes into the beef pot along with the coriander, cloves, cayenne, and garam masala.
Add the rice and simmer gently 20 to 25 minutes, stirring often, until the rice is tender and the soup has thickened.
Stir in the minced garlic, the red wine vinegar, and the dried dill and cook 3 more minutes.
Kill the heat, fold in the chopped cilantro, and taste for salt. Kharcho should be tangy, so add vinegar before you add salt.

name: Kielbasa Cabbage and Potato Skillet
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Dice the potatoes small and even so they cook through at the same rate. Core and slice the cabbage into ribbons, and slice the onion.
Heat the olive oil in your largest skillet and add the potatoes in a single layer. Let them sit undisturbed so they brown before you stir. Cover and cook until tender.
Push the potatoes to the side, add the sliced sausage coins, and brown them so the edges get some color.
Add the onion and cook until it softens, then stir in the garlic just until it smells good.
Pile in the cabbage a handful at a time, letting each addition wilt before adding the next.
Season with salt and black pepper, cover, and cook until the cabbage goes tender and sweet at the edges.
Stir everything together in your big pot, scraping the browned bits off the bottom of the skillet into it.

name: Kielbasa Mac and Cheese Bake
ingredients: Pasta Shells (Great Value): 28 oz dry (794 g)
Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 28 oz (791 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the oven to 375F and grease two large baking dishes. Boil the pasta shells to just under tender, since they will keep cooking in the oven, then drain them.
Slice the smoked sausage into coins and dice the onion.
Brown the sausage coins in a large pot until the edges darken, then add the onion and cook until it softens. Move both to a bowl.
Melt the butter in that same pot, whisk in the flour, and cook the roux for two minutes so it loses the raw flour taste.
Pour in the milk and the heavy cream slowly while whisking constantly, and keep whisking until the sauce thickens enough to coat a spoon.
Kill the heat and stir in the dijon mustard, the Worcestershire, salt, black pepper and most of the shredded cheddar. Adding cheese off the heat is what keeps the sauce from turning grainy.
Fold in the drained pasta and the sausage and onion, spread it into the baking dishes, top with the rest of the cheese, and bake until bubbling and golden.

name: Korean Beef Bibimbap Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice: 5.25 cups dry rice with water per your rice cooker or pot method.
Whisk the sauce: gochujang, soy sauce, rice vinegar, honey, and sesame oil.
Brown the ground beef in your big pot over medium-high until no pink remains, then drain. Stir in the sugar-free maple syrup, garlic powder, and half the sauce, and simmer 3 minutes.
Shred the carrots and thin-slice the cucumbers. Toss the cucumbers with a pinch of salt so they stay crisp in the fridge.
Fry or soft-scramble the 14 eggs. For meal prep that keeps, cook the yolks through.
Build each bowl: rice, beef, carrots, cucumber, one egg, a drizzle of the remaining sauce, and a sprinkle of green onion and sesame seeds.

name: Korean Beef Japchae Noodle Bowls
ingredients: Korean glass noodles (dangmyeon): 24.75 oz dry (700 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Slice the beef thin against the grain and marinate it with some of the soy sauce, sugar, garlic, sesame oil, and black pepper for at least twenty minutes.
Boil the Korean glass noodles until chewy and translucent, drain, rinse briefly, then cut through the pile a few times with scissors so they are manageable.
Toss the drained glass noodles with the remaining soy sauce, sugar, and sesame oil while still warm so they absorb the dressing.
Thaw and squeeze the frozen chopped spinach dry, then season it lightly with salt and sesame oil.
Cook the vegetables separately in the vegetable oil, one type at a time, so each keeps its own texture and color: onions, then carrots, then red bell peppers, then mushrooms.
Sear the marinated beef in the hot pan last, in batches, until browned and just cooked through.

Combine the dressed glass noodles, all the vegetables, the spinach, and the beef in your biggest bowl, toss thoroughly with your hands or tongs, and finish with the green onions and toasted sesame seeds.

name: Korean Braised Chicken and Potatoes (Dakdoritang)
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 7.75 lb (3500 g)
Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 9.75 tbsp (52 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Whisk the gochujang, soy sauce, honey, mirin, garlic, ginger, sesame oil, red pepper flakes, and black pepper into a sauce. Taste it and decide how hot you want the week to be, because this is your only chance to adjust.
Cut the chicken thighs into large pieces and toss them with about half the sauce.
Cut the potatoes and carrots into big chunks. Small pieces will disappear into the sauce over a long braise, and you want them to stay recognizable.
Put the chicken, potatoes, carrots, and onion into a wide heavy pot, pour the rest of the sauce over, and add the chicken broth. It should come about halfway up, not cover everything.
Bring it to a boil, then drop to a low simmer, cover, and cook 25 minutes.
Uncover, add the jalapeno, and simmer another 15 to 20 minutes while the liquid reduces into a thick glossy sauce. Stir gently so the potatoes stay whole.
Scatter the green onions over the top off the heat.

name: Korean Gochujang Ground Pork Rice Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice: 2 cups dry with water per your usual method.
Stir the sauce together: gochujang, mirin, sugar, soy sauce, and half the sesame oil.
Brown the ground pork in your big pot over medium-high heat, breaking it up, until no pink remains. Drain if needed.
Add the diced onion, garlic, and ginger and cook 3 to 4 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in the sauce and simmer 5 minutes until it glazes the pork and thickens slightly.
Finish with the rest of the sesame oil, most of the green onions, and the toasted sesame seeds. Serve over the rice with the last of the green onions on top.

name: Korean Ground Beef Rice Bowls
ingredients: Roasted Red Peppers (generic): 3 oz, from a jar (300 g)
Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 1 tsp (8 g)
steps: Brown the ground beef in a large skillet, breaking it apart, then drain the grease.
Stir in the minced garlic and cook until fragrant.
Add the gochujang, soy sauce, sesame oil, and brown sugar and stir into a glossy sauce.
Toss in the broccoli florets and cook until just tender.
Cook the rice while the skillet simmers.
Pile the beef and broccoli over the rice and serve.

name: Korean Ground Turkey Bowls
ingredients: Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 1/4 tsp crushed (2 g)
steps: Heat a little olive oil in a large skillet and brown the ground turkey.
Stir in the minced garlic and cook until fragrant, about a minute.
Add the teriyaki sauce and honey and let it simmer so the turkey soaks up the glaze.
Steam or microwave the broccoli florets until just tender and fold them in.
Serve over cooked white rice with the sauce spooned on top.

name: Korean Turkey Japchae
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the Korean glass noodles (dangmyeon) for 6 to 7 minutes until springy, drain them, rinse them cold, and cut through the pile a few times with scissors so they are eatable with a fork.
Beat the eggs, cook them thin in an oiled pan like a flat omelet, slide it out, and slice it into ribbons for the top.
Whisk the sauce: soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, and the minced garlic. Set it aside where you can reach it.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wide pan and brown the ground turkey, breaking it up, until it is cooked through to 165F, then move it to a bowl.

Stir-fry the vegetables in stages so each one keeps its own texture: mushrooms first, then onion and carrot, then red bell pepper, then the thawed and squeezed spinach. Move each batch to the bowl as it finishes.
Return everything to the pan with the noodles, pour the sauce over, and toss over medium heat for 3 minutes until the noodles turn dark and glossy and every strand is coated.
Kill the heat, fold in the green onions, and move it into your weighed pot.

name: Kuku Paka (Swahili Coconut Chicken Curry)
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 5 lb (2240 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Season the chicken thighs with salt and black pepper. Heat the vegetable oil in your largest pot over medium-high and brown them in batches until they have color on both sides, then set them aside. That browning is where half the flavor comes from.
Cook the diced onion in the same pot for 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic and grated ginger and cook one more minute.
Add the ground coriander, ground cumin, ground turmeric and cayenne pepper and stir them in the hot oil for 30 to 45 seconds until they smell toasted rather than dusty.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes, scrape the bottom clean, and let it cook down for 8 to 10 minutes until the tomato darkens and the oil starts to separate at the edges.

Stir in the coconut milk, return the chicken and its juices, and simmer uncovered for 25 to 30 minutes until the sauce thickens and the chicken reads 165F. Do not boil it hard or the coconut milk will split.
While it simmers, cook the rice and let it steam covered off the heat for 10 minutes.
Chop the chicken into bite-size pieces, stir it back in with the lemon juice and chopped cilantro, and fold the rice through the pot.

name: Lebanese Hashweh (Spiced Beef and Rice)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Melt about a third of the butter in your big pot and toast the broken spaghetti pieces, stirring, until deep golden. Watch it, they go from golden to burnt fast.
Add the rinsed rice and stir a minute to coat, then pour in the chicken broth. Bring to a boil, cover, drop to low, and cook about 15 minutes until tender. Rest 10 minutes off heat.
Meanwhile, brown the ground beef with the diced onion in a skillet with the remaining butter until no pink remains. Drain if needed.
Season the beef generously with cinnamon, allspice, salt, and pepper, and cook 2 more minutes so the spices bloom.
Fold the spiced beef into the rice gently with a fork so the grains stay fluffy.
Taste and adjust salt. Traditional move: top with extra toasted nuts if you have them on hand.

name: Loaded Beef Taco Skillet Bowls
ingredients: Seasoned Black Beans (Great Value): 6 cans (2366 g)
Sweet Whole Kernel Corn (Great Value): 2 cans (500 g)
Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 2 bags (280 g)
Red Bell Pepper (generic): 1/2 cup diced (260 g)
Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 1/4 tsp (2 g)
Black Pepper (Great Value): to taste (3 g)
steps: Brown the ground beef in a large skillet, breaking it up, then drain the grease.
Stir in the chili powder to season the meat.
Add the black beans, corn, diced zucchini, and tomato sauce and simmer until the zucchini is tender.
Stir in a little cooked rice to round out the skillet.
Sprinkle the shredded cheddar over the top and let it melt.
Spoon into bowls and serve.

name: Loaded Chicken and Potato Casserole
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 3.5 lb (1588 g)
Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 14 oz (396 g)
Hickory Smoked Bacon (Great Value): 1.25 lb (595 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the oven to 425 F. Cube the potatoes, toss them in your big pot with the olive oil, hot sauce, paprika, garlic powder, salt, and pepper, then spread on sheet pans.
Roast the potatoes 35 to 40 minutes, flipping once, until browned and crisp at the edges.
While they roast, cook the bacon until crisp, drain, and chop. Cube the chicken breast into bite-size pieces.
Cook the chicken in a bit of the bacon fat over medium-high, about 6 to 8 minutes, until it hits 165 F inside.
Lower the oven to 400 F. Combine potatoes and chicken in a 9x13 pan, top with the cheddar and bacon, and bake about 10 minutes until melted.
Finish with green onions. Keep the sour cream separate and add a spoonful when you reheat each bowl.

name: Loaded Ground Turkey Nacho Bake
ingredients: Seasoned Black Beans (Great Value): 2.8 cans (714 g)
Mexican Cheese Blend (Great Value): 22.25 oz (633 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet and brown the ground turkey, seasoning it with the garlic powder, salt, and black pepper as it cooks.
Add the diced onion and green bell pepper and cook 5 minutes, then stir in the drained black beans and the drained diced tomatoes and simmer 10 minutes until the mixture thickens.
The filling needs to be thick, not saucy. If liquid is still pooling in the pan, keep cooking, because a wet filling ruins the chips instantly.
Spread half the tortilla chips across two greased sheet pans or a large baking dish, then spoon half the turkey mixture over them and scatter half the cheese.
Repeat with the remaining chips, filling, and cheese, then add the sliced jalapenos across the top.
Bake at 400F for 12 to 15 minutes, only long enough to melt the cheese and warm everything through. Any longer and the chips give up.
Finish out of the oven with the chopped cilantro, dollops of light sour cream, and the salsa spooned over the top.

name: Loobia Polo (Persian Beef and Green Bean Rice)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, then parboil it in heavily salted water until the grains are soft outside and still firm in the center, and drain it.
Heat the olive oil in a pan and cook the diced yellow onion until golden, then add the garlic and cook until fragrant.
Add the ground beef, break it up, and cook until browned with no pink remaining.
Stir in the tomato paste, ground turmeric, ground cinnamon, salt, and black pepper and cook for a minute so the paste darkens.
Add the green beans and a splash of water, cover, and simmer until the beans are tender and the mixture is thick rather than wet.
Pour the vegetable oil into the bottom of a large heavy pot, then layer the parboiled rice and the beef mixture in alternating layers, mounding the rice toward the center.
Cover the lid with a clean towel, steam over the lowest heat until the rice is fluffy and a crust has formed on the bottom, then finish with the lemon juice.

name: Louisiana Red Beans and Rice with Sausage
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Slice the smoked sausage into coins and brown them in the vegetable oil in a large pot, then set them aside.
Add the diced onion, celery, and green bell pepper to the same pot and cook until softened and the bottom of the pot picks up color.
Stir in the garlic and the dried seasonings and cook for a minute so the spices bloom in the fat.
Add the kidney beans with their liquid and the chicken broth, then return the sausage to the pot.
Simmer uncovered for at least forty minutes, mashing some of the beans against the side of the pot to thicken the gravy.
Cook the rice separately according to the package while the beans simmer.
Fish out the bay leaves, season with salt and black pepper to taste, and serve the beans over the rice.

name: Malaysian Chicken Rendang Bowls
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 5.25 lb (2381 g)
Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 3.25 tbsp (18 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Blitz the onions, garlic, ginger, and lemongrass paste into a rough puree in a blender or food processor, working in batches.
Heat the vegetable oil in your big pot over medium and fry the puree 10 to 15 minutes, stirring often, until it darkens and the raw onion smell cooks off.
Stir in the cinnamon, cloves, garam masala, and red pepper flakes and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the cubed chicken breast and stir to coat, then pour in the coconut milk and sugar and bring to a simmer.
Simmer uncovered 35 to 45 minutes, stirring more often near the end, until the sauce reduces to a thick, deep brown coat on the chicken. Confirm the chicken reads 165 F.
Season with salt and pepper. The sauce should cling, not pool.

name: Marry Me Pork Chops over Pasta
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice: 3.75 cups dry with water per your usual method.
Pat the chops dry and season all over with the cajun seasoning, onion powder, garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
Sear the chops in olive oil in your big pot over medium-high, 3 to 4 minutes per side in batches, until they reach 145 F inside. Set aside to rest.
In the same pot, melt the butter and cook the garlic 1 minute. Pour in the chicken broth and scrape up the browned bits.
Add the heavy cream, chopped sun-dried tomatoes, oregano, and basil, and simmer 5 minutes until it thickens slightly.
Off the heat, stir in the parmesan until smooth. Slice the rested chops and return them to the sauce.
Serve the saucy pork over the rice.

name: Massaman Beef Curry with Potatoes
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Soak the dried arbol chiles in hot water for 15 minutes, then blend them with the onion, garlic, ginger, cilantro stems, and lemongrass paste into a smooth curry paste.
Heat the vegetable oil in a heavy pot and fry the paste over medium heat until it darkens and the raw smell burns off, about 8 minutes.
Add the ground cloves, cumin, nutmeg, garam masala, and cinnamon and toast for 30 seconds, then stir in the thick top layer of the coconut milk and let it bubble until the oil starts to separate.
Add the beef cut into large cubes and turn it in the paste, then pour in the beef broth and remaining coconut milk with the bay leaves. Bring it to a bare simmer.
Cover and cook on low for about 2 hours, until the beef is tender enough to cut with the side of a spoon.

Add the potatoes in chunks and simmer uncovered for 30 minutes more, then season with the fish sauce, sugar, and lime juice. Massaman should taste salty, sweet, and sour all at once, so adjust until all three are there.
Cook the rice, then stir the chopped peanuts into the curry off the heat.

name: Massaman Chicken Curry
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 2.75 lb (1270 g)
Red Curry Paste (Thai Kitchen): 11.25 oz (318 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Spoon the thick cream off the top of the unshaken coconut milk cans into your largest pot, keeping the thin liquid aside. Cook it with the olive oil over medium-high for 3 to 5 minutes until the oil separates.
Add the curry paste and the diced onion and fry them in that oil for 3 minutes, stirring, until the paste darkens and smells toasted.
Add the chicken cut into chunks along with the garlic and grated ginger, and turn everything until coated.
Pour in the reserved coconut liquid, then add the cubed potatoes and sliced carrots. Bring it to a simmer.
Stir in the peanut butter, brown sugar and fish sauce, then simmer uncovered 30 to 35 minutes until the potatoes are fork tender and the sauce has reduced and thickened around them.
Turn off the heat and stir in the lime juice, tasting as you go. Massaman should read sweet first, salty second and sour last, in that order.
Fold in most of the chopped peanuts and the cilantro, holding some of each back to scatter on top.

name: Mediterranean Beef Hummus Bowls
ingredients: Feta Cheese (Great Value crumbled): 7 oz (198 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice: 7 cups dry with water per your usual method.
Brown the ground beef in your big pot over medium-high until no pink remains, then drain.
Season the beef with the oregano, cumin, garlic powder, salt, and pepper and cook 2 more minutes so the spices wake up.
Chop the cucumber, halve the cherry tomatoes, and thin-slice the red onion.
Build each bowl: rice on the bottom, a scoop of hummus on one side, spiced beef on the other, then cucumber, tomatoes, red onion, olives, and feta.
Keep the fresh veg toppings in their own corner of the container so everything stays crisp until you eat.

name: Mediterranean Ground Turkey Bowls
ingredients: Black Pepper (Great Value): 1/4 tsp cracked (2 g)
steps: Heat a little olive oil in a large skillet and brown the ground turkey.
Add the chopped onion and sliced zucchini and cook until tender.
Stir in the diced tomatoes and let it simmer a few minutes to come together.
Season with salt, pepper, and whatever dried herbs you like, then take it off the heat.
Serve over cooked white rice with a big dollop of Greek yogurt on top.

name: Mediterranean Turkey and White Bean Stew Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the olive oil in a heavy pot and cook the diced onion for 6 minutes, then add the garlic and italian seasoning for one minute.
Add the ground turkey and brown it, breaking it apart as it goes, until it is cooked through to 165F.
Stir in the diced tomatoes, the chicken broth, the bay leaves, salt, and black pepper, and simmer 15 minutes.
Drain and rinse the cannellini beans and add them, then simmer another 10 minutes so they take on the flavor of the pot without falling apart.
Stir in the chopped kale and the sliced olives and cook 5 minutes more, just until the kale wilts and goes deep green.
Pull the bay leaves, add the lemon juice, and stir in most of the torn basil. Save some for the top.
Cook the rice, move it into your weighed pot, and keep the stew in its own pot for portioning.

name: Mexican Chipotle Pork and Beans
ingredients: Chipotle in Adobo (La Costena): 2 cans (400 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cube the pork shoulder, pat it dry, season generously with salt and black pepper, and brown it hard in the olive oil in a heavy pot, in batches so it sears rather than steams.
Cook the diced onion in the rendered fat until soft, then add the minced garlic, the ground cumin, ground coriander and ground allspice and stir for a minute.
Stir in the tomato paste and let it darken against the bottom of the pot for two minutes. That step is what separates a deep sauce from a flat one.
Add the chopped chipotles in adobo, the orange juice and the chicken broth, scrape the pot clean, and return the pork along with the bay leaves and dried oregano.
Cover and braise gently for about 3 hours, until the pork shreds under a fork and the liquid has reduced into a thick sauce.
Stir in the drained cannellini beans, simmer 15 more minutes so they take on the sauce, and pull out the bay leaves before portioning.

name: Middle Eastern Beef Kofta Bowls with Tzatziki
ingredients: Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 0.5 tbsp (3 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Make the tzatziki: grate about a third of the cucumbers, salt them, and squeeze out the water hard. Stir into the Greek yogurt with half the garlic, a splash of lemon juice, the mint, and a pinch of salt. Refrigerate.
Cook the rice: 4.5 cups dry with water per your usual method.
Grate one of the red onions and squeeze it dry. Mix it into the ground beef with the remaining garlic, cumin, cinnamon, allspice, red pepper flakes, salt, and pepper.
Shape the beef into small logs or ovals, about 3 per serving, and set them on foil-lined sheet pans.
Broil or bake at 450 F for 12 to 15 minutes, flipping once, until browned outside and cooked through with no pink in the center.
Slice the remaining cucumber and red onion and halve the cherry tomatoes.
Build each bowl: rice, kofta, tomato and cucumber salad, cilantro on top, tzatziki in its own corner or cup.

name: Middle Eastern Turkey and Green Bean Stew over Rice
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the turkey breast into bite-size chunks, pat them dry, and toss them with the flour, salt, and black pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a heavy pot over medium-high and brown the turkey in batches so it sears instead of steams, about 4 minutes a batch. Set it aside.
Drop the heat to medium, cook the diced onion for 5 minutes, then add the garlic, allspice, cinnamon, coriander, and paprika and stir for one minute until the kitchen smells like the dish already.
Stir in the tomato paste, let it darken for a minute, then add the diced tomatoes, the bay leaves, and enough water to loosen it into a stew.
Return the turkey, cover, and simmer on low for 45 minutes. In a slow cooker, this is the point where you set it on low for 6 hours and go live your life.
Add the green beans in the last 20 minutes so they stay tender instead of turning to mush, and check that the turkey has reached 165F.
Cook the rice, move it into your weighed pot, and keep the stew in its own pot for portioning.

name: Million Dollar Baked Spaghetti
ingredients: 1/3 Fat Cream Cheese (Great Value): 5.5 oz (159 g)
Reduced Fat Mozzarella (Great Value): 11.25 oz (316 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the spaghetti two minutes short of package time and drain.
Brown the ground beef and hot Italian sausage together in your big pot until no pink remains, then drain. Stir in the marinara and Italian seasoning and simmer 5 minutes.
Mix the ricotta, softened cream cheese, and sour cream in a bowl until smooth.
Layer in a greased 9x13 pan: half the spaghetti, all the cheese mixture, the rest of the spaghetti, then all the meat sauce.
Top with the mozzarella and bake at 350 F for 25 to 30 minutes until melted and bubbling at the edges.
Rest 10 minutes before cutting so the layers hold.

name: Mississippi Pot Roast Bowls
ingredients: Ranch Seasoning Mix (Hidden Valley): 5.75 tbsp (40 g)
Brown Gravy Mix (generic dry (USDA)): 1.25 oz (35 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Pat the chuck roast dry and season it with salt and black pepper. Set it in the slow cooker whole.
Sprinkle the ranch seasoning mix and the brown gravy mix evenly over the top of the roast. Do not stir and do not add water.
Lay the butter on top of the roast in slices so it melts down through the seasonings as it cooks.
Scatter the pepperoncini around and over the roast, along with a few spoonfuls of their brine.
Cover and cook on low for 8 hours. Resist opening the lid, since the roast is making its own liquid the whole time.
Shred the beef with two forks directly in the cooker and stir it through the gravy that has collected at the bottom.
Cook the rice separately and keep it plain, because the gravy is doing plenty.

name: Mongolian Ground Beef Bowls
ingredients: Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 1/4 tsp (2 g)
Beef Broth (Great Value): 1/4 cup (or water) (210 g)
Green Onions: 1/4 cup, thinly sliced (40 g)
steps: Brown the ground beef in a large skillet, breaking it up as it cooks, then drain any grease.
Add the minced garlic and grated ginger and stir for about a minute.
Pour in the soy sauce and honey and let it bubble into a glaze.
Add the broccoli florets and sliced red pepper and cook until just tender.
Cook the rice while the skillet finishes.
Spoon the saucy beef and vegetables over the rice and serve.

name: Moo Shu Pork Rice Bowls
ingredients: Oyster Sauce (Lee Kum Kee): 4.75 tbsp (84 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Slice the pork shoulder thin against the grain and toss it with some of the soy sauce, the cornstarch and the black pepper. Let it sit while you prep everything else.
Shred the cabbage, cut the carrots into matchsticks, slice the mushrooms, mince the garlic, and separate the green onion whites from the tops.
Beat the eggs and scramble them in a little of the vegetable oil until just set, then take them out and chop them roughly.
Get your largest pan very hot, add more oil, and stir fry the marinated pork in batches until it is browned and cooked through. Crowding the pan will steam the pork instead of searing it.
Add the garlic and the green onion whites, then the mushrooms, carrots and cabbage, and stir fry until the cabbage wilts but still has some bite left in it.
Return the pork, add the hoisin sauce, oyster sauce, the rest of the soy sauce and the chicken broth, and toss until everything is glazed.
Kill the heat, fold in the scrambled egg and the green onion tops, finish with the sesame oil, and serve over rice with warm tortilla strips standing in for the pancakes.

name: Morisqueta (Michoacan Pork, Rice and Beans)
ingredients: Mexican Cheese Blend (Great Value): 8.75 oz (250 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Cube the pork shoulder, season with salt and black pepper, and brown it in a heavy pot with a little olive oil, then add the bay leaves and enough water to nearly cover and simmer 90 minutes until tender.
While the pork cooks, blend the diced tomatoes, the husked tomatillos, the jalapeno, the arbol chiles, half the onion and the garlic into a rough salsa.
Cook the remaining diced onion in the pot, pour in the blended salsa, and let it fry and reduce for 15 minutes until it darkens and thickens.
Return the tender pork to the salsa and simmer another 20 minutes so the meat takes it on.
Cook the rice per the package, and warm the kidney beans with a little of their liquid so they stay soupy rather than dry.
Layer each portion rice first, then beans, then the saucy pork, and finish with the shredded Mexican cheese blend and chopped cilantro.

name: Moroccan Beef Tagine with Chickpeas
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the chuck into large cubes, pat dry, season with salt and pepper, and brown in batches in a heavy pot. Set the meat aside and leave the browned bits in the pot.
Cook the sliced red onion until soft, then add the garlic and ginger and stir for a minute until you can smell them.
Add the cumin, turmeric, paprika, and cinnamon and toast them in the oil for about 30 seconds. Blooming dry spices in fat is what separates a tagine from a bowl of dusty stew.
Stir in the tomato paste, then the diced tomatoes and beef broth, scraping the bottom clean. Return the beef with the bay leaves.
Cover and simmer gently for about 2 hours, until the beef pulls apart under a fork.
Add the carrots, drained chickpeas, brown sugar, and golden raisins and simmer uncovered another 30 minutes so the sauce thickens and the carrots go tender.
Finish off the heat with the lemon juice and a big handful of chopped cilantro. The acid at the end wakes the whole pot up.

name: Moroccan Turkey Kefta Tagine
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Grate about a third of the onions and mix them into the ground turkey with half the minced garlic, half the chopped cilantro, paprika, cumin, cinnamon, salt, and black pepper.
Roll the mixture into small meatballs, roughly an inch across. Small is the whole point here, so resist the urge to make them big.
Slice the remaining onions and soften them in the olive oil over medium heat for about 8 minutes, then add the rest of the garlic and cook one minute more.
Add the diced tomatoes with more paprika and cumin, season with salt and pepper, and simmer 15 minutes until the sauce pulls together.
Nestle the meatballs into the sauce, cover, and simmer 25 to 30 minutes until they are cooked through to 165F and the sauce is thick enough to hold a spoon track.
Cook the rice while the tagine simmers, then crack the eggs into wells in the sauce, cover, and cook 6 to 8 minutes until the whites are set.
Move the finished rice into your weighed pot and leave the meatballs, sauce, and eggs in the pan so you can divide them evenly on top.

name: Moussaka (Greek Beef and Eggplant Bake)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Slice the eggplant into thick rounds, salt them, and let them sweat in a colander for 30 minutes. Pat them dry, brush with olive oil, and roast at 425F until soft and golden, about 25 minutes. This step is what keeps moussaka from turning watery.
While the eggplant roasts, cook the onion in olive oil until soft, add the garlic, then brown the ground beef and break it up as it cooks.

Stir in the crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, beef broth, sugar, cinnamon, oregano, bay leaves, salt, and pepper. Simmer until it thickens and most of the liquid is gone, about 30 minutes. A wet meat sauce makes a sloppy bake.

Make the bechamel. Melt the butter, whisk in the flour and cook it for two minutes, then add the milk slowly while whisking until it thickens. Off the heat, stir in the parmesan and nutmeg, then temper in the beaten eggs so they do not scramble.
Scatter bread crumbs across the bottom of a large baking dish, then layer roasted eggplant, meat sauce, more eggplant, and pour the bechamel over the top so it reaches every corner.
Bake at 350F for 45 minutes, until the top is set and browned in patches. Let it rest at least 30 minutes before cutting. Cut it hot and the layers slide apart.
Cook the rice while the bake rests and put a scoop in the bottom of each container to round the meal out.

name: Musakhan (Sumac Chicken and Caramelized Onions)
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 3.75 lb (1750 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Slice all the onions thin. This is the longest part of the recipe and there is no way around it, so put on something to listen to and get it done.

Toss the chicken thighs with some of the olive oil, salt, black pepper, ground allspice, ground cinnamon, ground cumin, garam masala, ground nutmeg and a generous spoonful of the sumac. Let them sit while the oven heats to 425F.

Cook the sliced onions in the rest of the olive oil in your largest pot over medium-low heat for 30 to 40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they collapse into a soft sweet jam. Low and slow. If they are browning fast, the heat is too high.
Stir the bulk of the sumac into the cooked onions and let it cook another 5 minutes until they turn deep red and smell tart.
Roast the seasoned chicken on a sheet pan for 25 to 30 minutes, until it reads 165F and the edges are dark. Save every drop of the pan drippings.
Warm the flatbreads, tear them into large pieces, and toss them in your mixing pot with the pan drippings so they soak up the fat rather than staying dry.
Chop the chicken, fold it together with the sumac onions and the soaked bread, and finish with the chopped cilantro.

name: New Mexico Carne Adovada Pork Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Stem and seed the dried ancho and guajillo chiles, toast them briefly in a dry pan, then soak in hot water for 20 minutes until fully soft.

Blend the chiles with some soaking water, the garlic, white vinegar, soy sauce, sugar, ground cumin, dried oregano, dried thyme, salt and black pepper into a thick smooth puree, then strain out the skins.
Cut the pork shoulder into large cubes, coat every piece in the red puree, and refrigerate overnight.
Brown the diced onion in the vegetable oil in a heavy oven-safe pot, then add the pork with all of its marinade and the bay leaves.
Cover and braise at 325F for about 3 hours, stirring once an hour, until the pork shreds under a fork and the sauce has gone dark and thick.
Cook the rice per the package, then taste the chile for salt and pull out the bay leaves before you portion.

name: Nigerian Beef Stew over Rice
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the chuck roast into chunks and boil it with some of the onion, the bay leaves, thyme, curry powder, and salt until just tender. Strain and keep the stock.
Blend the diced tomatoes with the bell peppers, jalapeno, remaining onion, garlic, and ginger until smooth.
Heat the vegetable oil and olive oil in a wide pot and pour in the blended base. Fry it, stirring, until it thickens noticeably and the raw edge cooks off.
Stir in the tomato paste and keep frying a few more minutes so the paste loses its metallic taste.
Add the boiled beef, the reserved stock, and the beef broth. Simmer uncovered 30 to 40 minutes until the sauce is thick enough to sit on a spoon.
Taste and correct the salt and pepper. The stew should taste sharper than you think, because the rice will mute it.
Cook the rice separately and keep it plain.

name: Nigerian Chicken Suya Bowls
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 7 lb (3175 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Make the suya rub: whisk the peanut butter with the garlic powder, onion powder, smoked paprika, cayenne pepper, black pepper, salt and just enough chicken broth to loosen it into a thick paste that will spread.
Cut the chicken thighs into large strips and work the rub into every piece with your hands. Let them sit at least 30 minutes, or refrigerate overnight for a deeper crust.
Heat the oven to 450F and put a rack in the upper third. Brush two sheet pans with the vegetable oil so nothing welds itself to the metal.
Spread the chicken in a single layer with space between the pieces. Crowded suya steams and goes gray instead of crusting.
Roast 18 to 22 minutes, then run the broiler for 2 to 3 minutes at the end until the edges char in spots and the peanut rub sets into a crust. Watch it, because peanut burns fast.
While it roasts, cook the rice and let it steam covered off the heat for 10 minutes.
Chop the chicken into bite-size pieces, fold it into your mixing pot with the rice and the pan drippings, and stir the hot sauce through the whole batch.

name: No-Peek Pork Chop and Rice Casserole
ingredients: Cream of Mushroom Soup (Campbell's (USDA SR)): 3.5 cans (1043 g)
Onion Soup Mix (Great Value): 3.5 oz (99 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the oven to 350F and grease a large deep baking pan.
Stir the cream of mushroom soup together with the beef broth until smooth, then whisk in most of the onion soup mix.
Spread the uncooked rice evenly across the bottom of the pan and pour the soup mixture over it. Shake the pan flat, do not stir.
Season the pork chops with garlic powder, onion powder, salt and black pepper, and lay them across the top of the rice in a single layer.
Sprinkle the last of the onion soup mix over the chops, cover the pan tightly with foil, and get a good seal. Steam is what cooks the rice.
Bake for about 90 minutes without lifting the foil once, then rest 10 minutes before you uncover it.

name: One-Pan Sausage Bake with Potatoes and Onion Gravy
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the oven to 425F. Cut the potatoes into chunks, cut the carrots into thick batons, and cut the red onions into wedges.
Toss the vegetables with the olive oil, minced garlic, dried thyme, dried oregano, salt and black pepper, then spread them across two large sheet pans.
Nestle the bratwurst among the vegetables and roast until the sausages are browned and the vegetables are tender and caught at the edges.
Move the sausages and vegetables to a holding pan and keep them warm. Do not wash the roasting pan, because everything stuck to it is the gravy.
Set that pan across two burners, melt the butter in it, and scrape hard while it bubbles to lift all the browned bits.
Whisk in the flour and cook it for a minute, then pour in the beef broth in a steady stream while whisking until the gravy thickens.
Slice the sausages, combine them with the vegetables in your big pot, and pour the gravy over the top.

name: One-Pot Creamy Cajun Sausage Pasta
ingredients: Ziti Pasta (Great Value): 37.25 oz dry (1058 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Slice the smoked sausage into coins, dice the onion and red bell pepper, and mince the garlic.
Heat the olive oil in a large deep pot and brown the sausage coins until the edges take on color, then set them aside.
Cook the onion and pepper in the sausage fat until they soften, then add the garlic and the Cajun seasoning and stir for a minute so the spices bloom.
Pour in the chicken broth and the diced tomatoes and bring it to a boil, scraping the bottom clean.
Stir in the dry pasta, drop it to a simmer, and cook uncovered while stirring often so nothing sticks. The pasta will drink most of the liquid.
Whisk the cornstarch into a little cold water to make a slurry, then stir it into the pot and let it thicken for a minute.
Turn the heat low, return the sausage, and stir in the heavy cream and parmesan until the sauce goes smooth.
